a.text: '...Pavel, when there is danger, let the students leave first; they're easiest to identify, and likely to be considered less of a threat.'
'Their Tulskaya Technical School background makes them a higher priority for retention amongst the Infected. More numbers will be preserved if they get away.'
'All life is equal, of course, but sacrifice is inevitable in our work. We must all maximize the value of our lives for the cause.'
'Is it sad? Perhaps, but I do not have the luxury to wallow in sorrow. I must save my strength for anger and resistance.'
'That though the winter night be long and cold, have faith that the sun will shine again upon us equally.'

steps.name: Serious Student
steps.text: We're under the Second District. I remember the pillars marked with different colors in this passage. The exit is just ahead.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Are we just going to leave like this? What about your comrades who're staying behind?

steps.name: Serious Student
steps.text: If the Teacher and Pavel wanted us to leave, there must be a reason for it. Maybe they'll join us after fighting off the soldiers.

steps.name: Serious Student
steps.text: Shh—hide, someone's coming!

steps.name: Nervous Voice
steps.text: I saw someone. They must have went this way.

steps.name: Fierce Voice
steps.text: Don't get distracted. The other Infected don't matter, but the Generalik wants that Cautus found at any cost!

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: They're looking for... me?

steps.name: Robotic Voice
steps.text: Put down your weapons and you'll be spared!

steps.name: Robotic Voice
steps.text: Put down your weapons—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Turn that thing off.

steps.name: Deferential Soldier
steps.text: Y-Yes, sir!

steps.name: Deferential Soldier
steps.text: Turn off the speakers!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: There's fewer of them than I thought. Report.

steps.name: Deferential Soldier
steps.text: Yes, sir.

steps.name: Deferential Soldier
steps.text: At around 0300 hours, patrols found a group near the entrance to the Third District underground, apparently attempting to gain access to the residential district through the underground layer.

steps.name: Deferential Soldier
steps.text: We were outnumbered and the Marshal gave express orders not to harm Infected resources, causing us to lose track of some of them during the chase—
The killer presses his forehead, trying to soothe the splitting headache. He did not even look before swinging his sword.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: ...Someone who can talk better.

steps.name: Honest Soldier
steps.text: S-Sir!

steps.name: Honest Soldier
steps.text: There were more of them, but the patrol was short-handed, which allowed some of them to escape to the underground layer before we could confirm their identity.

steps.name: Honest Soldier
steps.text: The complexity of the underground layer makes tracking difficult. However, such a mistake should not have happened to begin with! It was our error!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You talk well and you know how to reflect. But that can't wipe clean the mistake, can it?

steps.name: Honest Soldier
steps.text: I-I—
The soldier reflexively glances at the still-warm body of his comrade lying on the ground.
He remembers the rumors: Generalik Anatoliy hates people who are talkative, people who overestimate themselves, and—
He hates liars.

steps.name: Honest Soldier & Calm Youth
steps.text: I will accept any punishment! / Perhaps I should explain.

steps.name: Honest Soldier
steps.text: You—what?

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Perhaps I should explain. I was directly involved, after all.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: A volunteering hero. What do you say to the charges of illegal gathering and resisting arrest that you and your friends are facing?

steps.name: Pavel
steps.text: Uchitel—

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: We did not resist arrest, because we were not gathering illegally. We have stayed to await justice.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Disappointing. I thought you'd have something new to say...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You bore me.
The Generalik turns around to face his soldiers before the calm youth has a chance to add anything.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: The Infected here refused to cooperate with you, didn't they?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: That's resisting arrest.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Sir!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: So it looks like you have no idea what to do if there are more than a couple of people resisting arrest.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Foolish and inflexible.

steps.name: Honest Soldier
steps.text: I accept any punishment—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: But I am magnanimous, and therefore I will show you what to do in these circumstances.
He moves.
The sword reaches the calm youth first. She would not have been able to avoid it, if someone had not pulled her out of the way.

steps.name: Pavel
steps.text: Argh—

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: —Pavel!
Even after the youth saw the sword take the life of a trained soldier, it is hard to accept that it has now taken one of their comrades just as easily.
The older miner did not have time to even utter a word. His eyes wide, his life frozen at the instant when he grabbed the youth's hands.
Only when there are screams and sobbing coming from behind does the youth realize what has transpired.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You make an example, like this. If killing one isn't enough, kill another, until they cooperate.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Mother's orders are important, of course, but under extraordinary circumstances such as these... does it matter whether the Infected is alive or dead?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I have made this decision. I, Anatoliy Svetlanov Buterin, take full responsibility for everything that happens here.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Now, before I cut off another head, who's going to tell me where your unruly friends have gone?

steps.name: Angry Miner
steps.text: You're mad! We won't—
The bodies on the ground lie as evidence of the two lives that have departed.
They dye the soles of the youth's boots red, but she does not look down. She looks up, straight into the Generalik's eyes.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Why the anger? You failed. That's the truth that no amount of killing will change.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: You claim you have the power to do anything, but you clearly can't get your way. You can't pry open our mouths with your sword, nor will you learn what you want to know.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: We have bought precious time for our comrades, while you thrash about, locked in the cage of your own anger.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: How dare you—
Fury twists the young man's visage. He wants to raise the butcher's knife again, but he cannot find a sliver of the fear he seeks in the youth's face.
And the whole lot of companions behind as well. Miners, farmers, nothing more, yet not a single one panics or flinches. He is unaccustomed to this reaction, or lack thereof.
Suddenly, Anatoliy realizes that he would simply be creating willing martyrs.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: ...Enough.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I've seen too many hackneyed tropes tonight.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Kill them all and clean up the mess. Then find—
Stop!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Hierda?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Hierda!

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I'm sorry, Anatoliy, I heard you were here—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You came back! You didn't flee!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: But why did you leave on your own?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You should be by my side always. This was your promise. Don't you know what a promise is?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I... I'm sorry for the misunderstanding.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: But... what's happening here?
Anatoliy tries to block Hierda's line of sight, but he can do nothing to mask the smell.
The scent of blood fills the air, even in the cold night.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...Anatoliy.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You promised not to kill more innocent people.
Hierda tries her best not to sound accusing. She does not want to anger Anatoliy, or further escalate the situation.
If only there was a manual on how to deal with a fickle, temperamental child with too much power over life and death...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Yes, I promised.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Anatoliy...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: But you didn't keep your end of the bargain. You left me.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I was only doing what I could while you slept. I said this to you, and you agreed.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: If I agreed to anything, it was only under the condition that you stayed with me.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...I don't know how we can carry on, if you keep changing the conditions—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: 'Don't know how we can carry on'?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You don't know how you can continue to stay by my side?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: No, listen to me—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Who planted such terrible thoughts in your mind? Who instilled such ideas in you—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You never questioned me before!
The sword is tossed aside, like a piece of scrap metal.
Anatoliy grabs the Cautus's slim shoulders. Then, amidst the surprised cries, his right knee hits the floor—
He kneels down in front of Hierda.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Oh—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I see you've suffered a malign influence. Tell me, what should I do? How can I change your mind?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Only I can realize your vision and bring glory to your great blessing—as long as you don't leave my side again.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I forgive you! I forgive all your mistakes, for leaving without a word.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: But please, don't leave me again... never again say these terrible words.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...I promise.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: As long as you promise never to kill another innocent...
As she picks her words, Hierda looks at the corpses lying in the middle of the road, and the Infected behind them.
Most of them have the same expressions on their faces, pained and wary.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Promise not to harm these Infected anymore... not to take any innocent lives.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: And I will promise in turn.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I'll stay by your side, and never leave again.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Lieutenant.

steps.name: Brave Servant
steps.text: ...Yes, Generalik?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Herd these scum back to the residential district and put them in an empty apartment.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Station an artillery regiment to keep a close eye on them.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Anatoliy?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Enough. Waste no more time on these dregs.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Let us go.
A lone figure sits in the warehouse. She has sat there through the night, until dawn begins to crack upon the horizon.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: 'Convince them that this is a matter of life and death'...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: How should I tell them...?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Zelgrad is not home...
Are you alright, Tonya?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Doctor Nadezhda Pavlovna...

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Sorry to keep you waiting. I've been getting a lot of emergency patients lately.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: You don't look well. Do you want something to calm your nerves?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: No, I'm fine. I appreciate everything you've done for me and my sister.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Her condition—

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Slow down, Tonya. You only brought her yesterday. I need to keep her condition under control first, and I still have questions for you.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: First, have similar symptoms appeared on other members of your family?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: No, not yet.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Just to be safe, I've entrusted my other siblings in the care of my neighbors, and checked for the source of infection according to your instructions.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Did you find it?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: There's only one possibility... my work jacket.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: It was issued to us at work, very thick and warm, so I put it around Nina those few days when the power went out... I shouldn't have done it!

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: She's at home all day. The only thing from the outside she could have come into contact with was that jacket.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: And I found a strange... powder on it when I checked it.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Powder?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Yes... I've never seen anything like it. It clung to the surface of the jacket like some kind of dust. Probably got on it while I was washing the clothes.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Whose clothes?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: The First Army... or rather, the First Army's researchers.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: You mean this has something to do with them?

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: ...We can't be sure yet.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: I know what you're thinking, Tonya, but right now there's no way to prove that the powder caused the illness.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: We'll have to get past that wall to find out.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: ...What will happen to my sister? What will the illness do to her?

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: I'm sorry, Tonya, but I haven't found anything similar to this in the books.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: I don't even know if it's just a singular incident or not, until more patients present themselves.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: I need more information about this strange new illness.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Elegant Voice
steps.text: Not a good feeling, is it, to be the only one awake?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Yes... I don't how I can make the others believe me.

steps.name: Elegant Voice
steps.text: Do not blame your friends.

steps.name: Elegant Voice
steps.text: Perhaps the land has never promised a future for them, not since the day they were born. They lost the courage to face the truth when happiness is dangled before them.

steps.name: Elegant Voice
steps.text: They will not thank the one who wakes them; they will blame you for ruining their dream.

steps.name: Elegant Voice
steps.text: When the future is full of despair, short-sightedness becomes a survival mechanism.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: I won't blame anyone... I know it doesn't seem like an immediate danger to them.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Wait, who are you?

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: I entered the city with the workers.

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: It wasn't my intention to disrupt your lives. I only came to see... an old friend.

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: Will she be here? I don't know... but she is rarely absent from spectacular occasions.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: I don't understand what you're saying. If there's nothing else—

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: How unfortunate. I do understand what you're saying... and what you're looking for.

spans.text: understand what you're saying... and what you're looking for.

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: I help the sleeping wake up, and make the weak strong.

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: Perhaps we can help each other... if you're willing.

steps.name: Elegant Woman
steps.text: Ah, I see I forgot to introduce myself—

steps.name: Koshelna
steps.text: Nice to meet you, Tonya. I'm a teacher. You may call me... Koshelna.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: (I think I lost them for real this time...)

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: (They were strictly aiming for my legs. Were they trying to immobilize me? Why didn't they shoot to kill?)

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: This is strange...

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: ...Ugh—
You're bleeding. The smell will draw pursuers.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: Who—
Let's keep it brief.
I know what you did, and I took care of some of your pursuers. At the current rate, your blood loss will send you into shock in three minutes.
I'll staunch your bleeding, then take you to a place that's... relatively safe.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: Who are you?
That's not important, and it's not like you have any other choice. Maybe you could try to stab me with your final breath... but would that be worth it?
Yes, that's more like it.
Keep quiet and conserve your energy.

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: I went and got a look, Red. Guess what?

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: The people that we ran into during the day and the folks that came in with them are all gone. Third floor through fifth floor are empty, and we hardly heard any footsteps.

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: I pried open a few locks just to make sure—

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Next time don't pry the locks, just knock.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: If they're anything like us, they wouldn't have been sleeping well the first night here.

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: Do you think they were taken away quietly like the previous group, or did they leave on their own?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: They're all miners. I gather they came from the north based on their outfits, but it's not clear whether they're from the Far North.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Let's find that industrial district mentioned in the intel.

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: I've never had the chance to ask, but do you really trust her that much? Maybe she wasn't really looking for the people who were taken away, and the intel's no good—

steps.name: Red
steps.text: She had many chances to get us killed and run away in the last two years. Why hasn't she done so?

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: How am I supposed to know what she's thinking?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Then shut your crap and don't let me hear that again, or you can go back to Nine and get your brain straightened out before coming out again.

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: ...I'm just being vigilant!

steps.name: Red
steps.text: You can, but only if you keep it to yourself at this stage.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: We're a very, very long way from having the luxury to settle old scores.

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: There's no one here...

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: Doesn't look like anyone's been working here for a while, either. It's been abandoned for a long time.

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: There are holes in the roof, and no equipment in sight. Looks like it's all been moved.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Industrial transfer.

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: When we first came, the soldier who acted as our guide told us that the previous tenants in our apartment were 'coincidentally' moved to other districts because of industrial transfer.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: No matter how 'coincidental', however, industrial transfer rarely takes place between different districts of a nomadic city.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: It's only megacities like Londinium and Grypherburg that have the demand and the capacity.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: And the corporations that performed industrial transfer in Londinium ultimately ended up moving their factories to smaller nomadic cities nearby, rather than other plates within the city.

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: How do you know this stuff?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: I read.

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: Fine...

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: But Zelgrad is just a medium-sized nomadic city... built upon a small-sized nomadic city, even, with unmapped expansion plates all over the place.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: There are a lot of questions, but we'll have to take them one at a time. There's no one here, nor in the dorms either. For now we can eliminate—

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: There's something up ahead—

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: Hey!

steps.name: Red
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Valiya
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Red
steps.text: You were right, next time, we should ask her what she's doing.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: She left someone here for us.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: It's typical Arts overload symptoms alright, with concurrent acute neurasthenia that makes single emergency medication less effective.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: There isn't much I can do other than prescribe sedatives and rest. She should refrain from using Arts until neurasthenia symptoms disappear.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: (Mutters) Thank goodness it wasn't that...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: It's nothing... say, your description of the symptoms was quite accurate, and you performed appropriate early treatment. I take it you have a bit of medical knowledge?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: 'Have a bit of medical knowledge'? I'm—

options: We don't have a doctor with us right now.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: I see... interesting, isn't it, to have so many 'doctors' arrive in Zelgrad lately.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Well, I guess I'm done here. I'll go back now—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: One moment, doctor!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Do you know anything else about the patient that I brought to your clinic?

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Just another poor soul too far gone to be helped... what else are you expecting me to tell you?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You were not surprised to see his symptoms.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You have seen others like him before, haven't you? How many other people have gotten the same illness here?

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Oripathy isn't the only thing that kills people in this land.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Besides, if something is being deliberately suppressed in Zelgrad, there's a reason for it, and I'm not going to look for trouble.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: I don't care what kind of doctor you are and why you came to Zelgrad. All I can tell you is that you shouldn't get involved in this stuff, and get out as soon as possible.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But you haven't left.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You haven't given up on helping the people here. Don't we share the same goal?

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Don't flatter me. I'm just scraping a living by doing what I know how to do.

options: We need a 'doctor' to help more people.
We trust any 'doctor' who's true to his or her duty.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: Hah... listening to that stuff is what cost me my license. Talk is cheap.

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: But fine... I still don't recommend that you get involved, but if you insist on investigating...

steps.name: Nadezhda
steps.text: One of the workers told me she took a piece of contaminated clothing from behind that wall...

options: The problem is with whatever lies behind that wall.
Does that strange powder have something to do with the Sarcophagus?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Doctor, I'm worried about what Amiya and that doctor described...

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Kal'tsit should have sealed the Sarcophagus five years ago.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: But Ursus is evidently hacking into the Sarcophagus very aggressively. I can't tell how far their research has progressed until I see the Sarcophagus myself.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: We can't afford to wait!

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I agree...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Raidian! The doctor said you have to rest!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Maybe I'm not the one who should talk, but shouldn't an elite operator exercise better judgment? Stay in bed.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I encountered powerful countermeasures while trying to probe what's happening inside the wall... it's well-defended...

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Besides the army's electromagnetic jamming... the whole city's magnetic field feels strange...

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: I'm sorry, Doctor... I can't help for now...

options: You took on a great risk for us.
No one could have done better.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: See? Listen to the Doctor, won't you? At least keep the blanket around you if you want to sit up. You were shivering just now.

options: But we do have to act quickly.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Based on what I saw, there are more strange things going on in Zelgrad than we thought.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: That gravely ill patient, the strange creature... the First Army must be hiding something terrible.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The First Army seems to be uncooperative towards the State Council. It's unlikely that they'll help us.

options: We can't sit around and wait.
We need to get through that wall.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: We have plenty of experience with situations like this! Leave the fighting to me!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: There's no such thing as an impregnable wall. Even the Armies of Ursus make mistakes.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: If you ever need someone to hack through a firewall, I'm right here!

options: It's very late. The garrison is probably on alert right now from all the commotion.
Let's look for a way to get through the wall during the day.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: Stop walking around like that, mudak! You're making my eyes hurt.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: It's been two days since they took the boss. When are you gonna go and get him out?

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: We have contingencies for situations like this. If he isn't back after one week, and there's no movement outside, Oleg will take over and we'll get ready to scram...

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: Are you out of your mind, svolotsch? Boss was telling us to be flexible, not run away at the slightest sign of trouble!

spans.text: Are you out of your mind,
Boss was telling us to be flexible, not run away at the slightest sign of trouble!

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: There isn't much difference.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: Of course there is. Don't you remember what we sing when we drink? 'Volniki have two paths to freedom, one they carve out with their swords, the other when they bleed and fall'—

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: We haven't done anything except bite like an obedient tuskbeast ever since we came here!

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: Kuznetsov's people are everywhere. We'll be detected immediately if we leave the base during the ceasefire. Right now, we need to keep the ship safe, and say nothing if anyone asks.

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: Oleg is already planning the retreat.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: At least we need to make those mudak pay the price for looking down on us.

spans.text: At least we need to make those
pay the price for looking down on us.

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: Is that more important than your life?

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: But we're not that lunatic Kuznetsov's pet tuskbeasts!

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: Even a tuskbeast will bite through its fence if cornered. Sirka would agree with me, if she was here.

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: But she's not.

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: You're right, though. We would be making a night visit to the flagship right now if Sirka was here.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: I'm starting to miss her. Should've learned those tricks of hers. Damn it all...

steps.name: Excited Officer
steps.text: Enough slacking! Scioppa's back, and in one piece!

steps.name: Excited Officer
steps.text: You have three minutes to hide your liquor and smokes and illegal Arts units—

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: We weren't drinking!

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: Or smoking. And we already hid our Arts units in case Kuznetsov sends another inspector. They took a bunch with them the last time, even ones that were still being repaired.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: Where's the boss, Oleg?

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: On deck! No one knows when he came back. He was standing there when I saw him.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: He just smiled when I asked, saying that everything's good. You know how people have been on edge since that incident in December.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: What's our next step? Are we still leaving?

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: The alarm's cancelled for now. Go back to your posts. I'll make another round; I'll let you know if anything happens—
There you are, Oleg.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: Boss!

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I want everyone who's awake out on deck.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: I have a important announcement to make.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Is everyone here?

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Everyone on the night shift.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Inform the others after the shift change.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: What's going on? The last time you called all hands was...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Remember the bomb that went off in Central recently?

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Who could forget? We could feel it all the way here. They say it left nothing except some strange-colored dust. The sight of the Viy eating someone could hardly be more terrible.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Hah, the Viy eating someone... you're right.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: That's the First Army's new weapon, which the people above really want to get their hands on. That's when the Special Tactics Formation comes in handy.
The man shrugs and turns around to face the others, which fall silent as he opens his mouth. His smile never leaves his face as he raises his voice.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: In other words, we just got a big job.

steps.name: Rowdy Soldier
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Are you saying—

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Yes, we're going to steal the First Army's new weapon.

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Wait a second. Going to the First Army's position means passing through the front lines, right? Which means we'll have to deal with the Second Army. Is that even possible?

steps.name: Oleg
steps.text: Or are we going to go around—

steps.name: Confused Soldier
steps.text: Or is it just a part of some kind of operation?

steps.name: Confused Soldier
steps.text: Maybe we just need to carry out our orders, like when we put down that mutiny.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: You're right. His High Excellency Marshal Evgeny Andrianov Kuznetsov has made arrangements for us to pass the Second Army's lines safely.

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: All we need to do is...

steps.name: Scioppa
steps.text: Advance.
